thread:
mike (eng-runtime): seeing a sharp rise in redis RPS and 504/503s since the 11:14 deploy. prefix cache miss rate jumped from ~5% to ~62% across p-* prefixes. graphs: https://grafana/redwood/d/prefix-cache

deploy-bot: deploy redwood/serving@release-2026-03-18 completed 11:14 UTC

arya (oncall): on it, scaling up read replicas now. can you paste the recent cache key change?

mike (eng-runtime): we rolled in a key normalization tweak earlier today:
```
cache_key = model + ':' + prefix_hash_v2(prefix)
# v2 includes tokenizer-based segmenting for stable collisions
```

asha (serving): hmm that should be backward compatible. but if tokenizer boundaries shifted for common prefixes, hit patterns could fragment. any profiler traces?

mike (eng-runtime): attached sampled traces show lots of near-identical prefixes mapping to different keys. KV lookup latency spiking too.

danielle (infra): I can throttle prefetch/autowarm and drop the background warmers to reduce write-amplification to redis. recommend emergency toggle: `kv_autowarm=false` and `prefetch_async=false`

arya (oncall): doing that now. toggling flags in staging -> canary -> global. please monitor.

sre-bot: alert resolved? No — redis rps still elevated but trending down after flag change on 11:28 UTC

mike (eng-runtime): after disabling autowarm, miss rate down to ~18% but still higher than baseline. kernel selection and batching heuristics unchanged in the deploy, confirmed by rollout trace. so not execution path regression. root looks key entropy / rekeying.

asha (serving): we rolled a small tokenizer tweak in the same release (tokenizer v1.4.2) that changes split points for punctuation-heavy prompts. likely increased key cardinality for popular prefixes.

danielle (infra): I rolled back the prefetch change and re-enabled autowarm partially with rate limit. setting `kv_autowarm_rate=0.2` for now. redis rps fell 70% from peak.

mike (eng-runtime): confirmed miss rate stabilized ~7.8% and tail latency back to normal at 11:45. logs show fallback to origin service for many hot prefixes during the window which explains backend overload.

asha (serving): immediate action: pin tokenizer to v1.4.1 for hot routes and add a migration plan for v2 keyspace (shadow warmup + mapping table)

arya (oncall): creating incident ticket and paging kernel/batching owners to review if any indirect effects.

mike (eng-runtime): blamelines: 1) tokenizer change increased key entropy without warmup, 2) simultaneous enable of new key format + autowarm made origin hit storm, 3) no Canary step for KV keyspace change.

deploy-bot: rollback of redwood/serving@release-2026-03-18 completed 11:52 UTC

danielle (infra): follow-ups: add canary for key-format feature flag, autoscale thresholds for KV write storms, and a safelist for hot prefixes to pre-warm on key-format swaps.

asha (serving): I'll open a doc with migration playbook (shadow warmup, tokenization stability tests, and metrics to watch: prefix-hit-rate, kv-write-surge, origin-503s).

mike (eng-runtime): for the perf team: add a smoke test that compares prefix-hit-rate before/after any tokenizer/kernel selection change and block rollout if delta > 3x baseline.

arya (oncall): incident mitigated, moving to post-incident review. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
